title: Hosted schema reconciliation and migration ledger
goal: Make staging schema, production migration history, generated types, and the launch migration ledger agree without destructive resets

in: Active Supabase migration chain and hosted staging/production migration history
Launch-required classification, one-at-a-time evidence, advisors, type generation, and forward repair
out: Destructive reset, forced replay, or automatic production migration application

acceptance_criteria: Every active migration has an explained staging and production history disposition
Launch-required migrations have one-at-a-time staging evidence, advisor output, and forward-repair instructions
Deferred migrations remain unapplied and are excluded from the launch manifest
Staging schema, generated types, migration ledger, and launch manifest have zero unexplained drift

evidence: Audit baseline: 294 active migrations exist, most validation manifests are still planned, zero are production-verified, and raw Management API applications created migration-history drift.

progress.summary: Partial batch implementation landed: added a hosted-history ledger for all 294 active migrations, launch-required/deferred classification, normal validation, strict release validation, and all-manifest scanning. The ledger honestly reports 287 unclassified migrations and unverified staging/production history.
completed: Added hosted-history-ledger.json and check-hosted-migration-ledger.mjs with normal and --require-reconciled modes.
Added active-chain, database-type source, and migration manifest validation tooling without resets or invented hosted evidence.
next_steps: Populate the ledger from authorized read-only staging/production history and classify the remaining active migrations under CP-051.
Regenerate database types from the exact staged schema and make strict ledger validation part of the release gate.
blockers: Strict release validation currently fails because 287 migrations remain unclassified and both environments default to unverified.
No authorized hosted schema/history access was available in this batch.
